 Where does LeBron James stand in the NBA record books?
 In his 24th season, LeBron James sits atop a number of categories in NBA history, and is still chasing more.
 Ben Lambert, for NBA.com
 November 15, 2026 9:17 PM LeBron James reached third on the all-time assist charts Sunday.
 LeBron James passed Jason Kidd (12,091) for third on the all-time assist charts Sunday, reaching 12,092 and further cementing his place as one of the great playmakers in NBA history. 
 James’ vision has been key to his success. He’s been dominant in the high pick-and-roll, either driving to the rim or kicking the ball out to teammates, and always has his eyes open for cutters. 
 “It means I had a lot of great teammates. You’ve got to have teammates that put the ball in the hole. My job is just to try to put it on-time, on-target,” James said after passing Kidd Sunday. “I love the history of the game. I love the players that came before me. It’s super honoring.” 
 James said he always enjoyed watching his teammates score from his first day playing basketball. 
 “I always got joy and a kick out of seeing my teammates score. It was a feeling that felt really good,” said James. “The energy behind the pass, I understood how it could be infectious to the team.” 
 He began his career with 5.9 assists per game as a rookie, then never dipped that low again, averaging between 6.0 and 10.2 ast in each of his other 23 seasons.  
 That 10.2 ast mark won him the assist title in 2019-20, as well as spurred the Los Angeles Lakers to the championship. 
 But where does the King rank elsewhere in NBA history? 
 Points:
 James is famously the all-time leading scorer in NBA history , finishing Sunday’s action with 43,606 points. No other player has cracked 40,000 points; only eight are over 30,000. 
 Rebounds:
 He’s 23rd on the rebounding list in NBA history, pulling down 12,174 boards through Sunday. 
 Charles Oakley, who twice cracked 13.0 reb and finished second to Michael Cage in a famously-close rebounding race in 1987-88 , is next on the list with 12,205. 
 The legendary Dennis Rodman, who won seven consecutive rebounding titles from 1992 to 1998, is just behind him at 11,954. 
 James is the Cleveland Cavaliers’ all-time franchise leader in rebounds with 6,190. 
 Blocks:
 LeBron finished Sunday with 1,193 blocks — 66th in NBA history.  
 Bo Outlaw and Adonal Foyle are tied 1,193, while Chris Webber stands just ahead at 1,200. 
 Steals:
 James is sixth on the all-time steals list with 2,430. Gary Payton is ahead, with 2,445, with Maurice Cheeks behind at 2,310. 
 LeBron is also the all-time leader in games played, minutes played, field goals made and attempted, and seasons played. 
 He’s second in free throws made and attempted, fifth in triple-doubles and sixth in 3-pointers made. 
 In this game, there’s only one King, and he’s not done putting his mark on the NBA record books.
